newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares fall amid political uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares fall amid political uncertainty.

text.p: Israeli shares closed sharply lower on Thursday in nervous trading amid rising political uncertainty, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.97 percent, or 5.02 points, to 249.27 on an all-share turnover of 99 million shekels against 86 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.73 percent lower at 259.40.

"Trading was nervous today but the market is still showing strength. The fact that the indices lost less than two percent on such a day shows that there is no panic," said Eli Nahum head of trading at Zannex Securities.

Police stunned Israel on Wednesday by saying they recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netnyahu be charged with fraud and breach of trust over the appointment of political crony Roni Bar-On as attorney general in January.

"The prime minister has no intention of going now to elections or resigning or suspending himself," spokesman Shai Bazak told Israel Radio. "The prime minister is confident of his innocence. We are all sure of it."
Legal experts say a decision to charge the prime minister would force him to resign and prompt new elections.

"The Maof rose from 250 in March to 265 last Tuesday and today's decline can also be seen as technical correction. The scandal was only the trigger for today's decline," said Baruch Glicksberg at Clal Insurance.
"The main question is whether Netanyahu resigns and if he does, when it will happen. All the uncertainty is bad for the market. A resignation may lead to a rise of the market," Nahum said.
Glicksberg added that foreign investors used the opportunity to buy shares.

"It is clear that there is no panic but it is difficult to predict where the market is going. The economic situation is not clear, the future of the peace process is not clear either and there is much political uncertainty," Glicksberg said.

The most active shares were Israel Discount Bank, which closed unchanged at 340 agorot on volume of 10 million shekels; Koor Industries, which closed unchanged at 30,649 agorot on turnover of 7.3 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which lost 1.5 percent to 18,459 agorot on volume of 5.5 million shekels.
